title: Steve Jobs: Apple Innovation
description: Design obsession, startups, and the company that put computers in pockets.

questions.question: Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak founded Apple on April Fools' Day of what year?
questions.hint: The same year as America's bicentennial celebration
questions.explanation: A third co-founder, Ronald Wayne, sold his 10% stake back less than two weeks later for $800, a slice later worth billions. No joke.

questions.question: The 1976 startup's first mass-produced hit computer, launched in 1977, was called what?
questions.hint: The Roman numeral for two, this computer had color graphics and was hugely successful
questions.explanation: Mostly Wozniak's design, it shipped with color graphics, and the pioneering VisiCalc spreadsheet made it a business tool. Its profits funded the Mac era and the 1985 fight that pushed Jobs out.

questions.question: After the Apple II era and his ouster, Jobs founded what computer company later acquired by Apple?
questions.hint: It was literally what came 'after' Apple for Jobs, spelled with unusual capitalization
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee built the first web server and browser on a NeXT at CERN. Apple paid $429 million for NeXT in 1996, and Jobs came along with the deal.

questions.question: NeXT's operating system became the foundation of the software inside what device Jobs unveiled in January 2007?
questions.hint: A phone that starts with 'i' and put the internet in everyone's pocket
questions.explanation: Jobs teased "an iPod, a phone, and an internet communicator" before revealing one device. Prototypes crashed so often that engineers scripted a "golden path" for the demo.

questions.question: Even after the iPhone, most of Jobs's fortune came not from Apple but from what animation studio he bought in 1986?
questions.explanation: Disney bought it for $7.4 billion in stock in 2006, making Jobs its largest individual shareholder. Not bad for a Lucasfilm graphics unit he got for about $10 million.

imageHint: 🍎 Think different - from garage startup to tech empire 📱

deeperMode.title: The Perfectionist's Obsessions
deeperMode.description: Perfectionism and controversy behind the brand

questions.question: Jobs was famous for his demanding perfectionism. What did he reportedly make his team redesign 67 times for the first iPhone?
questions.hint: The container that holds the product - he wanted the 'unboxing experience' to be perfect

questions.question: What Zen Buddhist practice did Jobs follow that influenced Apple's minimalist design philosophy?
questions.hint: A practice of mental focus and awareness that values simplicity and presence
